query: Footnote's Drawer Footnote has sat on one catalogue drawer for a week and hisses at anyone who comes near it. The label underneath him says OVERDUE, ELEVEN YEARS. The head librarian says whoever finds that book is welcome to the trick of finding books. Find out what he's guarding You read the card around his tail. A book on wards, borrowed by a Professor Thorne, eleven years ago. Footnote looks at you as if you've finally asked the right question. Shelve around him You shelve around Footnote for the rest of the shift. He watches every book you put away, as if marking them.

results.title: Footnote's Drawer
results.excerpt:
Footnote's Drawer
Footnote has sat on one catalogue drawer for a week and hisses at anyone who comes near it. The label underneath him says OVERDUE, ELEVEN YEARS. The head librarian says whoever finds that book is welcome to the trick of finding books.
Find out what he's guarding

results.title: Still Guarding It
results.excerpt:
Still Guarding It
Footnote is still on the overdue drawer, eleven years and half a year now, and the head librarian has started leaving his saucer there. When you pass, he stops washing and stares at you, as if you'd promised him something and he has been very patient about it.
G

results.title: Eleven Years Overdue
results.excerpt:
Eleven Years Overdue
Tonight the shelves are moving. Somewhere in the wandering section is the book, eleven years overdue, and every book you touch tries to fall open at the wrong page. {flag(index_fish): Footnote is on your shoulder.|You're on your own.}
Find the page
Your hand

results.title: Bribing the Cat
results.excerpt:
Bribing the Cat
Footnote won't move from the drawer for less than fish. Good fish, from the village, not the refectory's. The head librarian says this is "between you and the cat".
Buy him a proper herring
Footnote eats the herring slowly, looking at you the whole time, then step

results.title: Overdue
results.excerpt:
Overdue
Professor Thorne returns a book that is eleven years overdue. The fine, by library rules, is forty crowns. He looks at you. You look at the ledger.
Waive the fine
"Hm," says Thorne. You can't tell if you've earned his respect or lost it.
Enforce the rules
A long silence.
